⚠️\\n\\n### plan_012 θ-Conditioning 失败\\n- logit θ 与 total score 相关性 0.9986 → 单维 θ 分层 ≡ 总分分层\\n\\n### plan_014 Within-Subject 前置检查：C% = 38.1% (>25%)\\n- 5 个高 C% subjects 的 within-subject temporal C% 均 >25%（31-45%）\\n- Within vs cross-subject matching 差异仅 -2.4pp → 信号对 matching 不敏感\\n- **结论**：temporal DIF 渗透到每个 subject 内部，不是 between-subject 能力差异的伪影\\n- Bifactor 方向因此否定（D010）\\n\\n### plan_013 Q3 局部独立性：温和但存在\\n- Within-subject mean Q3 = 0.009（低于 0.20 阈值）\\n- 但 11.3% within-subject pairs |Q3|>0.20（vs 2.2% cross-subject，5x）\\n- 最严重: moral_scenarios 34.2%, world_religions 18%, marketing 17.5%\\n- 不太可能单独解释 31% FPR\\n\\n### plan_016 Within-Subject Semi-Synthetic：DIF 在 subject 内也有效 ✅\\n- Cross-subject matching FPR 完全稳定（ΔFPR=0.000），4/5 subjects ΔTPR>0.3\\n- Within-subject matching FPR 膨胀 +0.067 to +0.281（matching variable 包含注入 items）\\n- **结论**：within-subject 38% C% 是真实 temporal DIF，方法论有效\\n\\n### 综合推导：31% temporal FPR 不是 artifact\\n证伪链完整：1D θ 无效 → within-subject 仍高 → bifactor 否定 → Q3 不是主因 → **这是 genuine temporal DIF**（2023→2024 模型在特定 items 上的真实差异性表现变化）。DIF 方法有效但无法区分 contamination-DIF 和 capability-DIF。\\n\\n## D012: plan_017 Downstream Impact — DIF Items ≠ 噪声 ⚠️\\n\\n### Hypothesis 被证伪但发现更有价值\\n- **假设**: 移除 DIF items → 排名更稳定 → DIF 标记了 problematic items\\n- **实际**: DIF 移除造成 **更大** 排名扰动（z = -8 to -49σ, 21/21 条件）\\n- DIF items 是浓缩的差异化信息载体，不是噪声\\n\\n### 关键数字\\n- Full vs stable-only: ρ = 0.996-0.999（排名本身极鲁棒）\\n- DIF items 跨代准确率变化 = full benchmark 的 1.09×, stable = 0.96×\\n- Top beneficiaries: phi-3, llama-3 衍生（+700-850 rank positions）\\n- Top hurt: mistral merge/slerp 模型（-400 to -587 rank positions）\\n\\n### 对论文的启示\\n- DIF items 不是\\\"要清洗的坏题\\\"——是\\\"揭示模型代际差异的诊断工具\\\"\\n- 支持 characterization narrative > cleaning narrative\\n- \\\"Stable-only benchmark\\\" 不是\\\"更好的 benchmark\\\"，而是\\\"不同视角的 benchmark\\\"\\n\\n## 数据源 (2026-05-20)\\n\\n### METABENCH (Kipnis et al., ICLR 2025) ⭐\\n- GitHub: https://github.com/adkipnis/metabench\\n- Zenodo: https://zenodo.org/records/12819251 (620MB)\\n- MMLU 12,508 items, 5,219 模型\\n\\n### D002: preproc.rds diff/disc 是 CTT 不是 IRT\\n- diff = 0.75 × p_correct, disc = rpbis\\n- 实际 IRT 在 crossvalidate.R 用 mirt::mirt() slope-intercept\\n\\n### Li et al. # Plan 004 Step 3: GSM1K Contamination Gap × DIF Flag Correlation

## Summary

**Core finding**: Pearson r = −0.478 (p = 0.005). The correlation is significant and exceeds the |r| > 0.3 threshold, but the direction is **negative** — opposite to the contamination hypothesis. Models with larger GSM8K–GSM1K gaps show *less* advantage on DIF-C items, not more.

## Data

| Component | Count |
|-----------|-------|
| Matched models (in both GSM1K paper and MetaBench response matrix) | 33 |
| DIF-C items (standard matching, ETS class C) | 249 |
| Non-DIF items (ETS class A + B) | 1070 |
| Excluded: tiiuae/falcon-180B-chat (not in MetaBench) | 1 |

## Main Analysis

| Metric | Value | p-value |
|--------|-------|---------|
| Pearson r | −0.478 | 0.005 |
| Spearman ρ | −0.403 | 0.020 |

All 33 models (except Deepseek-math-7b-rl) show **negative DIF advantage** — accuracy on DIF-C items is consistently lower than on non-DIF items. Models with larger contamination gaps show even more negative DIF advantage.

## Control Analyses

### Partial Correlation (controlling GSM8K overall accuracy)

| Metric | Value | p-value |
|--------|-------|---------|
| Partial r | −0.385 | 0.027 |

The correlation survives after controlling for overall accuracy, ruling out the confound that "strong models do better on everything."

### Permutation Test (n = 1000)

| Metric | Value |
|--------|-------|
| Observed r | −0.478 |
| Null mean | −0.007 |
| Null SD | 0.197 |
| Null 95% CI | [−0.383, 0.366] |
| Empirical p (two-tailed) | 0.014 |

The observed correlation falls outside the null distribution's 95% CI. The DIF-C item set produces a significantly stronger negative correlation with contamination gap than random item subsets of the same size.

### DIF-C Directionality Analysis

DIF-C items split by direction (α_MH relative to 1):

| Subset | n | Mean advantage | r with gap | p |
|--------|---|----------------|------------|---|
| DIF-C favoring focal (newer, α>1) | 78 | +0.031 | −0.143 | 0.429 |
| DIF-C favoring reference (older, α<1) | 171 | −0.194 | −0.347 | 0.048 |

The overall negative correlation is driven primarily by the 171 reference-favoring DIF-C items. High-contamination models struggle disproportionately on items where older models perform relatively better. The 78 focal-favoring items show no significant relationship with contamination gap.

## Outlier Analysis

### Cook's Distance (top 5)

| Model | Cook's D | Gap | DIF Advantage |
|-------|----------|-----|---------------|
| Deepseek-math-7b-rl | 0.300 | −0.022 | +0.003 |
| GPT-2-xl | 0.161 | 0.004 | −0.001 |
| Smaug-2-72B | 0.129 | 0.061 | −0.069 |
| Gemma-2b-it | 0.075 | −0.001 | −0.033 |
| Deepseek-llm-67b-base | 0.071 | 0.093 | −0.155 |

Deepseek-math-7b-rl is the most influential point (negative gap, near-zero DIF advantage).

### Leave-One-Out

| Removed model | r without | Δr |
|---------------|-----------|-----|
| Deepseek-math-7b-rl | −0.374 | −0.105 |
| Smaug-2-72B | −0.537 | +0.058 |
| Gemma-2b-it | −0.438 | −0.040 |
| Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.2 | −0.516 | +0.038 |
| GPT-2-xl | −0.442 | −0.037 |

Removing Deepseek-math-7b-rl weakens the correlation to r = −0.374, but it remains significant (still > 0.3). No single point drives the result; the correlation is robust.

## Model Family Observations

| Family | n | Mean gap | Mean DIF advantage |
|--------|---|----------|--------------------|
| Smaug | 2 | 0.065 | −0.128 |
| Phi | 4 | 0.037 | −0.174 |
| Gemma | 5 | 0.051 | −0.143 |
| Llama/CodeLlama | 9 | 0.028 | −0.117 |
| Mixtral | 4 | 0.028 | −0.143 |
| DeepSeek | 2 | 0.036 | −0.076 |

No single family dominates the trend. Phi models show high DIF disadvantage but moderate gaps. Gemma models cluster at moderate gap + moderate DIF disadvantage. The correlation is not an artifact of one family.

## Interpretation

### Against the contamination hypothesis

The original hypothesis predicted **positive** correlation: contaminated models should gain disproportionate advantage on DIF-C items. The observed **negative** correlation (r = −0.478) contradicts this.

### What DIF-C items capture

DIF-C items are not simply "contaminated items." They are items with large differential functioning between temporal cohorts. 171/249 DIF-C items actually *disadvantage* newer models (α_MH < 1). These represent items where older models perform disproportionately well, possibly reflecting:

1. Items testing patterns that were better represented in older training data
2. Items where newer model training (including potential contamination) disrupts general problem-solving strategies
3. Items that genuinely discriminate between different capability profiles across generations

### The negative correlation means

Models with higher contamination gaps (suspected contamination) do *worse* on DIF items — they show a narrower advantage pattern concentrated on non-DIF items. This is consistent with contamination producing a uniform boost on "normal" items while failing on items with atypical difficulty characteristics.

### Success criteria assessment

| Criterion | Result |
|-----------|--------|
| \|r\| > 0.3 (breakthrough) | ✅ \|r\| = 0.478 |
| Direction as hypothesized | ❌ Negative, not positive |
| Survives controls | ✅ Partial r = −0.385, permutation p = 0.014 |

**Verdict**: The effect size meets the breakthrough threshold, but the direction inverts the contamination narrative. DIF-C items do not flag contaminated content — they flag items where contaminated models are actually *weaker*. This is still a strong, publishable finding: it demonstrates that DIF analysis captures genuine measurement anomalies orthogonal to contamination, supporting DIF as a tool for identifying construct-relevant item differences rather than data leakage.

## Output Files

- `gsm1k_dif_correlation.csv` — per-model data (33 rows)
- `fig_gsm1k_dif_correlation.png/pdf` — scatter plot with regression
- `fig_gsm1k_dif_perm_null.png` — permutation null distribution
- `plan_004_step3_gsm1k_dif_correlation.py` — analysis script

## 任务：GSM1K Bootstrap Confidence Intervals

### 背景
plan_004 Step 3 分析了 33 个模型的 GSM8K-GSM1K contamination gap 与 DIF advantage 的相关性，得到 Pearson r = −0.478 (p=0.005)。审稿人要求报告所有关键相关系数的 95% CI。

### 方法
1. 读取 plan_004 Step 3 的数据。数据在 `artifacts/plan_004/gsm1k_dif_correlation.csv`（33 行，含 gap, dif_advantage, acc_dif_c, acc_non_dif 等列）。
2. 对以下相关系数做 BCa (bias-corrected and accelerated) bootstrap (n=10000, seed=42)：
   - (a) Pearson r between gap and dif_advantage: r = −0.478
   - (b) Spearman ρ between gap and dif_advantage: ρ = −0.403
   - (c) Partial Pearson r controlling for GSM8K overall accuracy: r = −0.385
3. 同时计算 plan_001 的 domain ρ = 0.307 的 bootstrap CI（如果 plan_001 数据可用且适用）。
4. 报告每个系数的：point estimate, 95% BCa CI, bootstrap SE, bootstrap distribution percentiles (2.5%, 50%, 97.5%)。

### BCa Bootstrap 实现
```python
from scipy.stats import pearsonr, spearmanr
import numpy as np

def bca_bootstrap_ci(data_x, data_y, stat_func, n_boot=10000, alpha=0.05, seed=42):
    """BCa bootstrap confidence interval."""
    rng = np.random.RandomState(seed)
    n = len(data_x)
    
    # Observed statistic
    theta_hat = stat_func(data_x, data_y)
    
    # Bootstrap distribution
    theta_boot = np.zeros(n_boot)
    for i in range(n_boot):
        idx = rng.choice(n, size=n, replace=True)
        theta_boot[i] = stat_func(data_x[idx], data_y[idx])
    
    # Bias correction (z0)
    z0 = scipy.stats.norm.ppf(np.mean(theta_boot < theta_hat))
    
    # Acceleration (jackknife)
    theta_jack = np.zeros(n)
    for i in range(n):
        idx = np.concatenate([np.arange(i), np.arange(i+1, n)])
        theta_jack[i] = stat_func(data_x[idx], data_y[idx])
    theta_dot = np.mean(theta_jack)
    a = np.sum((theta_dot - theta_jack)**3) / (6 * np.sum((theta_dot - theta_jack)**2)**1.5)
    
    # BCa percentiles
    z_alpha = scipy.stats.norm.ppf([alpha/2, 1-alpha/2])
    p1 = scipy.stats.norm.cdf(z0 + (z0 + z_alpha[0]) / (1 - a*(z0 + z_alpha[0])))
    p2 = scipy.stats.norm.cdf(z0 + (z0 + z_alpha[1]) / (1 - a*(z0 + z_alpha[1])))
    
    ci_lower = np.percentile(theta_boot, p1*100)
    ci_upper = np.percentile(theta_boot, p2*100)
    
    return theta_hat, ci_lower, ci_upper, np.std(theta_boot), theta_boot
```

对 partial r，每次 bootstrap resample 时重新计算 partial correlation（残差化后的 Pearson r）。

## 任务：GSM1K Bootstrap Confidence Intervals

### 背景
plan_004 Step 3 分析了 33 个模型的 GSM8K-GSM1K contamination gap 与 DIF advantage 的相关性，发现 Pearson r = −0.478 (p=0.005)。审稿人要求所有关键相关系数附 95% CI。

### 方法

2. 对以下相关系数做 BCa bootstrap (n=10,000)：
   - (a) Pearson r between gap and dif_advantage（应得 r ≈ −0.478）
   - (b) Spearman ρ between gap and dif_advantage（应得 ρ ≈ −0.403）
   - (c) Partial Pearson r controlling for GSM8K overall accuracy（应得 r ≈ −0.385）。需要读取或计算 GSM8K overall accuracy per model。如果 CSV 中有 gsm8k_acc 列直接用，否则从 response matrix 算。
3. 额外：如果 plan_001 报告中提到 domain ρ = 0.307，也对此做 bootstrap（但这可能在不同数据集上，如果数据不在 plan_004 中则跳过）

### BCa Bootstrap 实现
```python
from scipy.stats import pearsonr, spearmanr
import numpy as np

def bca_bootstrap_ci(x, y, stat_func, n_boot=10000, alpha=0.05, seed=42):
    rng = np.random.RandomState(seed)
    n = len(x)
    theta_hat = stat_func(x, y)
    
    # Bootstrap distribution
    theta_boot = np.zeros(n_boot)
    for i in range(n_boot):
        idx = rng.choice(n, size=n, replace=True)
        theta_boot[i] = stat_func(x[idx], y[idx])
    
    # Bias correction
    z0 = scipy.stats.norm.ppf(np.mean(theta_boot < theta_hat))
    
    # Acceleration (jackknife)
    theta_jack = np.zeros(n)
    for i in range(n):
        idx = np.concatenate([np.arange(i), np.arange(i+1, n)])
        theta_jack[i] = stat_func(x[idx], y[idx])
    theta_dot = np.mean(theta_jack)
    a = np.sum((theta_dot - theta_jack)**3) / (6 * np.sum((theta_dot - theta_jack)**2)**1.5)
    
    # BCa percentiles
    z_alpha = scipy.stats.norm.ppf(alpha/2)
    z_1alpha = scipy.stats.norm.ppf(1 - alpha/2)
    
    a1 = scipy.stats.norm.cdf(z0 + (z0 + z_alpha) / (1 - a*(z0 + z_alpha)))
    a2 = scipy.stats.norm.cdf(z0 + (z0 + z_1alpha) / (1 - a*(z0 + z_1alpha)))
    
    ci_lo = np.percentile(theta_boot, 100*a1)
    ci_hi = np.percentile(theta_boot, 100*a2)
    
    return theta_hat, ci_lo, ci_hi
```

the DIF effect is unique or replicable by simpler item selection heuristics.

# Bootstrap Confidence Intervals for GSM1K Correlation Analysis

BCa (bias-corrected and accelerated) bootstrap with n_boot = 10,000, seed = 42.

## Results

| Statistic | Estimate | 95% BCa CI | p-value | n_boot |
|-----------|----------|------------|---------|--------|
| Pearson r (gap vs dif_advantage) | -0.478 | [-0.714, -0.155] | 0.0049 | 10000 |
| Spearman ρ (gap vs dif_advantage) | -0.403 | [-0.687, -0.031] | 0.0201 | 10000 |
| Partial r (gap vs dif_advantage | gsm8k_acc) | -0.385 | [-0.640, -0.058] | 0.0296 | 10000 |

## Interpretation

- All three CIs exclude zero, confirming statistically significant negative correlations.
- The Pearson r point estimate (-0.478) matches the Step 3 report value (−0.478).
- The Spearman ρ (-0.403) matches the Step 3 report value (−0.403).
- The partial r (-0.385) matches the Step 3 report value (−0.385).

## Method

BCa bootstrap adjusts for both bias and skewness in the bootstrap distribution.
Jackknife acceleration factor corrects for non-constant variance across the sample.
Sample size: n = 33 models. Resamples: 10000.
